q: When was Una National Park established?
a: Una National Park was declared in 2008, when the Law on Una National Park was passed. The public enterprise that manages the park was registered in early 2009, and its founder is the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The park protects the upper course of the Una and its tributaries, the Unac and the Krka.

q: How big is Una National Park?
a: According to the Law on Una National Park and the official website npuna.com, the park covers 19,800 hectares, or 198 km². Some sources quote larger figures because they include the buffer zone. It is considered the largest national park in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Within the park are the Una and Unac canyons, waterfalls, forests and several villages, including Kulen Vakuf and Martin Brod.

q: Where is Una National Park?
a: The park lies in the far north-west of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the border with Croatia, and under the Law on Una National Park its entire area falls within the City of Bihać. It is around thirty kilometres from Plitvice Lakes National Park. Bihać is the nearest large town and the usual starting point for trips into the park.

q: How far is Una National Park from Bihać?
a: The nearest park entrance is Lohovo, about 15 minutes' drive from Bihać. The Gorjevac entrance is 14 km from Bihać centre on the road towards Bosanski Petrovac. Allow around 45 minutes to an hour to drive to Štrbački buk, and about an hour to Martin Brod, roughly 50 km away.

q: How many entrances does Una National Park have?
a: The park has six numbered entrances: Gorjevac (1), Ćukovi (2), Ćelije (3), Račić (4), Martin Brod (5) and Lohovo (6). According to the park, the Račić entrance is not yet in use. The first three lead to the Štrbački buk zone, Martin Brod leads to Milančev buk, and Lohovo is the closest to Bihać.

q: Which Una National Park entrance is best for Štrbački buk waterfall?
a: Most visitors use entrance 3, Ćelije, on the roughly 8 km road from Orašac to Štrbački buk. The road is partly tarmac and partly gravel, and only cars, motorbikes and minibuses with up to 35 seats are allowed. The Gorjevac entrance has a longer gravel section, about 14 km, with a 30 km/h speed limit.

q: Can you get to Štrbački buk by coach?
a: Large coaches are not allowed on the road from Orašac to Štrbački buk because it is too narrow. Cars, motorbikes and minibuses with up to 35 seats are permitted, and the park helps large organised groups arrange transport. Group transfers on the Orašac – Štrbački buk stretch are paid separately to local operators.

q: What is the Ćukovi entrance to Una National Park?
a: Ćukovi is entrance number 2, for walkers and cyclists only. It is on the local road leading towards Štrbački buk, Kulen Vakuf and Martin Brod. Motor vehicles are not allowed through. You can drive from Bihać to the entrance and continue on foot or by bike from there.

q: Where is the Lohovo entrance to Una National Park?
a: Entrance number 6, Lohovo, is on the left bank of the Una and is the closest park entrance to Bihać. It has an information and control point in a wooden house. From here a forest trail runs from Dvoslap to Troslap past a series of smaller waterfalls on the Una. The trail is ideal for a gentle riverside walk, and the entrance is about 15 minutes' drive from Bihać.

q: What are the main sights in Una National Park?
a: The main sights are Štrbački buk, the largest waterfall on the Una, and Martin Brod with the Milančev buk group of waterfalls. There is also Kulen Vakuf with the old Ostrovica fortress, Rmanj Monastery where the Unac meets the Una, and the Troslap and Dvoslap waterfalls near Lohovo. Most of them can be seen in one or two days from Bihać.

q: Where do I buy tickets for Una National Park?
a: Tickets are sold at the entrances to the visitor zones, for example at the entrances towards Štrbački buk and at Martin Brod. According to the park's price list, services are paid in cash or by bank transfer to the park's account, so bring cash in convertible marks (KM) to the entrance. Check the current price list and payment options on the official website npuna.com.

q: How much does a ticket to Una National Park cost?
a: Ticket prices are set by the park and vary by season, visitor age and location, so we do not list them here. There are separate tickets for Štrbački buk and Martin Brod, as well as combined and family tickets. The current price list is published on the park's official website, npuna.com.

q: Do children pay to enter Una National Park?
a: Children under 7 get in free, and a reduced child rate applies to children aged 7 to 14. There are also family packages and discounts for pensioners and people over 65. Check the exact amounts in the price list on npuna.com.

q: Who gets free entry to Una National Park?
a: According to the park's price list, free entry applies to children under 7, residents of certain villages within the park, owners of property in the visitor zones, journalists with a press card, and guides and drivers of pre-booked groups. Curiously, anyone named Una also gets in free with an ID card. Conditions may change, so check them on npuna.com.

q: What does the Štrbački buk ticket include?
a: A single ticket for the Štrbački buk zone is valid for a full day in the Štrbački buk – Lohovo zone and includes visitor insurance. Toilets at Štrbački buk are charged separately. Group transport from Orašac is not included in the price. If you are also planning to visit Martin Brod, a combined ticket is worth considering.

q: What does the Martin Brod ticket include?
a: The ticket for the Martin Brod zone is sold at entrance number 5 and covers the Milančev buk and Jalački buk waterfalls. There is also a combined ticket for Štrbački buk and Martin Brod if you plan to see both. Prices are in the price list on npuna.com.

q: Is Una National Park open all year round?
a: You can visit the park all year round, and the price list distinguishes between low season (December, January and February), pre-season, mid-season and high season in July and August. In winter the gravel access roads are sometimes harder to drive and facilities are more limited. Check conditions on npuna.com before a winter visit.

q: When is the best time to visit Una National Park?
a: For powerful waterfalls, April, May and June are best, when there is most water. For swimming and rafting the best period is from late May to late September, while autumn brings colourful forests and fewer visitors. July and August are the busiest months, so arrive in the morning.

q: Can you swim in Una National Park?
a: Swimming in the Una inside the park is allowed only at designated spots and only while the entrances to the visitor zones are open. It is forbidden to swim within 50 metres upstream or downstream of waterfalls or to walk on tufa barriers. Swimming in the park's other rivers, such as the Unac, is not allowed.

q: Are barbecues allowed in Una National Park?
a: Lighting fires in the park is forbidden outside designated areas. Visitors may only use the fixed barbecues at the picnic area by Štrbački buk and at the Lučica picnic area in Martin Brod. If you want to barbecue without restrictions, a riverside cottage is a better choice, for example one of the houses on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Are dogs allowed in Una National Park?
a: Dogs are allowed in the park only with their owner and always on a lead. On minibus or coach transfers they must wear a muzzle. Dogs are not allowed in religious buildings or on the boardwalks at Štrbački buk and Martin Brod. General park rules also apply to dogs, so do not let them disturb wildlife.

q: Can I fly a drone in Una National Park?
a: Drones may not be used in the park without prior permission from the park management. Commercial photography without a permit is also forbidden. To request permission, contact the park management via the details on npuna.com. The same rules apply everywhere in the park, including Štrbački buk and Martin Brod.

q: Can you camp in Una National Park?
a: Camping is only allowed at official campsites and designated areas. The Lučica picnic area in Martin Brod has covered tables and benches, and there are private campsites around the park. If you prefer a proper bed, you can find accommodation in Bihać or on the Una at apartmanibihac.com.

q: What activities can you do in Una National Park?
a: In the park you can go hiking, cycling, rafting, kayaking and canoeing, fishing with a permit, and diving on a designated stretch. Boating is allowed on the Štrbački buk – Lohovo, Martin Brod – Kulen Vakuf and Troslap – Dvoslap stretches with a special ticket. There are also walks to the waterfalls and visits to fortresses and the monastery.

q: Can you fish in Una National Park?
a: Fishing is only allowed in zones designated by the park and with a valid fishing permit. In the fly-fishing sections all fish must be released, and elsewhere the rules limit the number and size of fish you can keep. Check the conditions and types of permit on npuna.com. Hunting or disturbing wild animals in the park is forbidden.

q: Is there parking in Una National Park?
a: Yes, there are car parks at the main sights, including one at the end of the road to Štrbački buk and one at the Gorjevac entrance. In summer, especially at weekends, the car park by the waterfall can fill up. Arrive early in the morning if you are travelling in July or August. At Martin Brod, park in the village near entrance number 5 and the Lučica picnic area, following the signs.

q: Is Una National Park suitable for children?
a: Yes, Štrbački buk and Martin Brod have well-maintained boardwalks and viewpoints, so they are suitable for families with children. Hold children's hands on the wooden paths and by the water, as the edges are slippery, and swimming near the waterfalls is not allowed. Children under 7 do not pay for entry.

q: How much time do you need for Una National Park?
a: Half a day is enough for Štrbački buk, including the drive from Bihać and a walk around the viewpoints. If you also want to see Kulen Vakuf, Ostrovica and Martin Brod, allow a full day. For a more relaxed visit with swimming and rafting, stay two or three days in Bihać or on the Una.

q: Can I get to Una National Park from Croatia?
a: Yes, from Croatia you can reach the park via the Izačić – Ličko Petrovo Selo, Užljebić or Strmica border crossings, depending on where you are coming from. From the Plitvice direction the most convenient is Izačić, after which you continue through Bihać to the park entrances. Bring your passport or ID card for the border.

q: How far is Una National Park from the Plitvice Lakes?
a: According to the park, Una National Park is about thirty kilometres from Plitvice Lakes National Park. From Plitvice to Bihać is a 35 to 40-minute drive via the Izačić crossing, then roughly another 45 minutes to an hour to Štrbački buk. You can visit both parks from a base in Bihać, with accommodation on apartmanibihac.com.

q: What wildlife lives in Una National Park?
a: The park is home to bears, wolves, lynx, otters and chamois, and more than a hundred bird species have been recorded. Around thirty fish species live in the Una and its tributaries, including trout and grayling. There are bear warning signs on the road to Štrbački buk, so drive slowly.

q: What cultural sights are there in Una National Park?
a: The park contains the remains of medieval and Ottoman fortresses, such as Ostrovica and Havala near Kulen Vakuf, and the Orthodox Rmanj Monastery near Martin Brod. Kulen Vakuf has an Ottoman-era mosque and an old bazaar quarter (čaršija). Traces of the Iapodes and the Roman period can also be found in the park and along the Una.

q: Is there a visitor centre in Una National Park?
a: The park has information points at the Gorjevac, Ćelije and Martin Brod entrances, where you can also buy souvenirs and maps. The park administration is in Bihać, at Bosanska 17d, and is open on weekdays. Contact details are on the official website, npuna.com.

q: What is the official website of Una National Park?
a: The official website of Una National Park is npuna.com, which publishes the price list, visitor rules, entrances and contact details. Check ticket prices and any changes to access there before your visit. You can also email the park administration at info@npuna.com. The administration's phone number is +387 37 221 528, and it is open on weekdays from 8:00 to 16:00.

q: What is not allowed in Una National Park?
a: In the park it is forbidden to drop litter, light fires outside designated areas, camp outside designated sites or leave the paths. It is also forbidden to damage trees and rocks, disturb animals or ride quad bikes off marked tracks. Dogs must be kept on a lead, and drones may only be flown with permission.

q: Can you cycle through Una National Park?
a: Yes, cycling is one of the park's activities, and the Ćukovi entrance is specifically for walkers and cyclists. The gravel roads to Štrbački buk and Martin Brod are suitable for mountain and trekking bikes. In summer set off early, as there is little shade or water on the longer stretches.

q: Is the road to Una National Park paved?
a: The main roads from Bihać to Orašac, Kulen Vakuf and Gorjevac are tarmac, but the access roads to Štrbački buk are still partly gravel. Beyond Kulen Vakuf towards Martin Brod there is also a short gravel section. Drive slowly, especially on narrow stretches where two cars can barely pass.

q: Where should I stay to visit Una National Park?
a: Bihać is the most practical base, as it is close to all the park entrances, and the Plitvice Lakes are only about 35 km away. For peace by the river choose a house in Lohovo, near the Lohovo entrance; for town life, an apartment in the centre. On apartmanibihac.com a whole apartment, up to 100 m², costs from €25, or 50 KM, per night, roughly the price of a single room in Bihać.

q: Is Una National Park a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
a: Una National Park is not on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The tufa waterfalls at Martin Brod have been on Bosnia and Herzegovina's Tentative List since 2019. The park has launched an initiative to include Štrbački buk in the nomination. Until any listing, the park is protected as a national park under the law of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

q: How far is Martin Brod from Štrbački buk?
a: From Štrbački buk you drive back along the access road to Orašac and continue via Kulen Vakuf to Martin Brod. The drive usually takes about 45 minutes, depending on the gravel sections. You can see both in one day if you set off in the morning. Kulen Vakuf is on the way, where you can stop at the old Ostrovica fortress.
